text: Which tyrosine kinases are expressed in every tissue, sit at the plasma membrane, and are targets of approved small-molecule drugs?
plan: Protein class: Enzymes / Tyr protein kinases AND Tissue category (RNA): any / Detected in all AND Subcellular location (ICC): Plasma membrane AND Protein class: FDA approved drug targets / Small molecule drugs
understanding: The query asks to identify genes that are tyrosine kinases, ubiquitously expressed across all tissues, localized to the plasma membrane, and targeted by approved small-molecule drugs.

trail.why: Tyrosine kinases correspond directly to the subclass 'Tyr protein kinases' under the enzyme class.
"Detected in all" corresponds directly to being detected across every tissue in the dataset, while leaving Level 1 unrestricted applies the filter globally.
The question specifically requires the protein to sit at the plasma membrane, without restricting the reliability or additional annotation features at level 2.
The requirement specifically calls for targets of approved small-molecule drugs, which corresponds to the 'FDA approved drug targets' class and 'Small molecule drugs' subclass.

requirements.why: This field covers enzyme classes including kinases and their subclasses.
This field classifies genes by RNA specificity and distribution across human tissues, including ubiquitous expression categories such as detected in all tissues.
This field identifies the cellular compartment observed by immunofluorescence, which includes 'Plasma membrane'.
This field includes classes for drug targets, specifically small-molecule drug targets.
